newsitem.title: USA: State Street Q3 driven by global investing.
newsitem.headline: State Street Q3 driven by global investing.

text.p: A boom in cross-border investing is fueling rapid growth at State Street Boston Corp, chief financial officer Ronald O'Kelley said in a telephone interview.

Discussing third-quarter results reported earlier Wednesday, O'Kelley noted that non-U.S. assets under custody for U.S. customers are up 39 percent from a year ago, and assets under custody for non U.S customers are up 49 percent.
Non-U.S. assets managed for all customers were up 67 percent from a year ago.

He said the company, which had $2.7 trillion in assets under custody and $280 billion under management at the end of the quarter, has experienced strong growth in the Pacific Rim since its international diversificaton was launched. But he said it has found Europe to be its strongest overseas market due to the developed financial infrastructure.
In the 1996 third quarter ended September 30 State Street Boston reported net income rose 14 percent to $73.6 million and earnings per fully diluted share rose 17 percent to $0.90 from a year ago.
O'Kelley noted that the compunded grwoth rate in earnings per share is 20 percent for the first three quarters of 1996, compared to the company's historic growth rate of 15 percent compounded.
He declined to comment on earnings forecasts. According to the Zack's service, the mean estimate among analysts for all 1996 is $3.51 per share, and the mean for 1997 is $3.96 per share.
State Street Boston's shares were up 1/8 to 58-3/8 in afternoon trade.
